question: Which shrinkage method reduces small effect sizes to exactly zero?

answers.feedback: Right. LASSO sets small effects to zero, so it also selects variants.
Ridge shrinks every effect but never reduces any to exactly zero.
With p = 1 (infinitesimal model), every variant keeps a non-zero, proportionally shrunk effect.

question: In LDpred, what does the parameter p (called ρ by Khera et al.) represent?

answers.answer: The proportion of variants assumed to be causal (with non-zero effects)
answers.feedback: Right. High p is the infinitesimal model (many small effects); low p assumes few variants with larger effects.

answers.answer: The P-value threshold for including SNPs
answers.feedback: LDpred does not use a P-value threshold; p is the assumed fraction of causal variants.

answers.answer: The LD (r²) between pairs of variants
answers.feedback: LD comes from the reference-panel LD matrix, a separate input.

question: Khera et al.'s type 2 diabetes score used LDpred with ρ = 0.01. Out of 1,000,000 variants, how many does this assume are causal? (Press Enter after your answer.)

answers.feedback: That would be ρ = 0.001 (the coronary artery disease score). For ρ = 0.01: 0.01 × 1,000,000.
Multiply the assumed proportion of causal variants by the number of variants: 0.01 × 1,000,000.

question: Why does LDpred need an LD matrix?

answers.answer: So that correlated SNPs carrying the same signal are not counted twice
answers.feedback: Right. GWAS estimates for SNPs in LD reflect the same causal variant; the LD matrix lets LDpred account for that.

answers.answer: To calculate the P-values of each SNP
answers.feedback: P-values come from the GWAS summary statistics.
Effect alleles come from the summary statistics; LD describes correlations between variants.

question: According to the lecture, what most improves the accuracy of a PRS?

answers.answer: The power of the GWAS used for the effect sizes (data >> methods)
answers.feedback: Right. A larger, better-powered base GWAS matters more than the choice between C+T, LASSO or LDpred.

answers.answer: Always using the newest shrinkage method
answers.feedback: Shrinkage methods often perform only a little better than clumping and thresholding. Data matter more.

answers.answer: Including as few SNPs as possible
answers.feedback: The best number of SNPs depends on the trait; it is chosen empirically in validation data.
